source.title: Deep Learning Through A Telescoping Lens: A Simple Model Provides Empirical Insights On Grokking, Gradient Boosting & Beyond
source.authors: Alicia Curth; Alan Jeffares; M. van der Schaar

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The authors explicitly replicate the CIFAR-10, single-hidden-layer neural-network double-descent experiment of [BHMM19] and report test-error results across a model-width sweep.
record.gate_note: The study also reports results on grokking over training time and additional width sweeps. Cited double-descent and epoch-wise results from other work are background, not rows. The effective-parameter plots are recorded as related findings, but they do not test whether one measure predicts peak locations across all axes or whether plotting error against that measure yields an ordinary U-shape.
record.test_reason: The study replicates the single-hidden-layer ReLU CIFAR-10 cat-vs-dog width sweep of BHMM19 (an original source) with the same method and measure. It reports test error across width, and adds MNIST (with and without label noise) and MNIST-1D sweeps. It also reports a temporal double-descent-like curve and test-time effective-parameter curves, which the authors say reconcile deep double descent with the U-curve.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the telescoping model lets them use test-time effective parameters for neural networks. In the double-descent sweeps, p_test falls past the interpolation threshold while p_train rises, which they say resolves the tension with the classical U-curve and quantifies benign overfitting. Grokking likewise coincides with train/test effective-parameter divergence. On MNIST, double descent appears only when label noise is added.
record.recipe_differences: The CIFAR-10 size-sweep experiment is explicitly presented as a replication of [BHMM19], using a single-hidden-layer ReLU network and binary image classification. The study also adds effective-parameter measurements and reports supplementary MNIST and MNIST-1D experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The MNIST size-sweep result changes with added label noise: no double descent without added noise and a characteristic shape with 20% label noise. In the polynomial grokking experiments, the timing and form of generalization vary with epsilon; in the MNIST grokking experiments they vary with initialization scale and sigmoid use.

fits_no_version.finding: Train and test effective parameters diverge when test error improves after interpolation, both across width and during grokking; later divergence coincides with later generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Divergence between train-time and test-time effective parameters tracks benign overfitting in double descent and grokking.

record.problems: The main size-wise replication and additional settings are limited to selected datasets and architectures. Numerical curve values are presented in figures rather than stated in the text. The authors report four random seeds for the size-sweep experiments and mean standard errors, but the text does not provide numerical uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported test-error conditions were omitted. Background results cited from other work were not extracted. Figures 4, 11–13 include temporal and additional grokking settings, but only the explicitly described double-descent-like epsilon = .05 temporal result is retained as a V2 row; the other grokking results report delayed or quick generalization rather than a stated epoch-wise double-descent curve.

untested.parts: Only single-hidden-layer fully connected networks on small binary tasks (8×8 CIFAR-10, MNIST, MNIST-1D); no deep or convolutional architectures.
No epoch-wise replication of the original ResNet/CNN setting; only one polynomial-regression grokking setting shows a rise-then-fall.
No capacity sweeps for non-neural model classes in this study; tree and boosting results are cited from CJvdS23.
There is no test that one complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs and samples.
Multiple peaks and the effect of optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
Test error is not plotted against effective parameters directly.

missing.what: The authors' explicit statement that their effective-parameter result shows the CJvdS23 fold-back-to-U-curve effect in deep learning, which bears on V7.
missing.locator: Section 4.1 (double descent paragraph); Appendix A.1, end of 'Double descent' paragraph

missing.what: Epsilon = .05 result: p_test first exceeds p_train, then drops below it, alongside the temporal rise and fall in test error.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source, but it replicates an experiment from BHMM19. The first and second authors also wrote CJvdS23, the U-turn paper on which the V7-style argument rests. Curve values are figure-only, so all states rest on the authors' descriptions. Uncertainty is reported as standard errors over 4 seeds (5 for the polynomial task).

versions.untested_parts: No broad range of architectures or datasets; the main replicated size sweep is a single-hidden-layer ReLU network on CIFAR-10, with additional MNIST and MNIST-1D settings.

The paper does not replicate the original epoch-wise double-descent experiment. Its own temporal evidence is principally from grokking experiments; the reported epsilon = .05 result is described as double-descent-like.
Training-sample size is not varied near an interpolation threshold.
No general capacity sweep across model classes; the gradient-boosted-tree comparison concerns irregular test inputs, not double descent.
The study measures effective parameters on train and test data, but does not test whether a single measure predicts peak location across size, training time, and sample size.
The study compares a task with and without added label noise. It does not test multiple peaks or triple descent, nor whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
It does not plot test error against effective parameter count to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
